extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item Associated Press newspaper page reporting wartime news and human-interest features (military actions, policy statements, and service recruitment). Contains narrative prose that includes criteria for suitability in submarine service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submarine service recruitment / suitability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical and psychological fitness requirements for submarine service: "physical requirements are strict because our subs need good, tough men ... Men with physical and mental stamina." Also: "Resourceful young men with intestinal fortitude are required," and volunteers only are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context and elaboration from the article: submarine patrols last many weeks ("the men go on patrols lasting many weeks and 90 per cent of them never see the sun during this time"), require a different psychology from surface or air service, and crews must be largely self-reliant ("submarines are all on their own and can not depend on assistance from any source once they have left their base for a patrol"). Practical recruitment notes: only volunteers are allowed; many applicants are rejected for failing to meet strict standards; recruiters should stress both hardships (confined quarters, long patrols, exposure to charges and other weapons) and attractions (safety via submerging, recent 50% pay boost, improved living conveniences aboard, specialized training useful for postwar civilian jobs).
